sentences.en: And one of the things that we've seen in just the last few years in this field is a real change in the way we talk about food.
sentences.zh: 在过去几年里，我们在这个领域看到的一件事是，我们谈论食物的方式发生了真正的变化。

sentences.en: When I was in graduate school, we were learning all about carbs and fats and protein and vitamins and minerals and how we break these nutrients down and use them in our bodies.
sentences.zh: 当我在读研究生时，我们学习的是碳水化合物、脂肪、蛋白质、维生素和矿物质，以及我们如何分解这些营养素并将其用于身体。

sentences.en: Nobody at that time was talking about how foods were processed.
sentences.zh: 当时没有人谈论食物是如何加工的。

sentences.en: And now, just in the last few years, we're seeing a lot of attention on how food processing might affect our health and especially this category of ultra-processed foods.

sentences.en: What happened was that tobacco companies, R.J.

sentences.en: So, the tobacco-owned products were much more likely to be something that scientists call hyperpalatable.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由成瘾科学家定义的术语，用来描述一种含有至少两种高水平营养素的食物。

sentences.en: And what's hyperpalatable?
sentences.zh: 要么是高脂肪和高盐，要么是高碳水化合物和高盐，或者是高脂肪和高糖。

sentences.en: So, this is a term that was defined by addiction scientists to describe a food that has high levels of at least two nutrients.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些营养素组合，你在自然界中通常找不到一种同时含有两种高水平营养素的食物，或者说未加工的食物。

sentences.en: It's either high fat and high salt or high carbohydrate and high salt or high fat and high sugar.
sentences.zh: 科学家认为，当我们吃一种高度可口的食物时，它只会让我们更难停止进食。

sentences.en: So, these pairs of nutrients, like you wouldn't normally find a food in nature or like an unprocessed food that is high in two of those nutrients at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们想要更多，你知道，我们会伸手去拿奥利奥包装袋里的下一块饼干。

sentences.en: And scientists think that when we eat a food that's hyperpalatable, it just makes it harder for us to stop eating it.

sentences.en: We want it more and, you know, we reach back into the package of Oreos for another cookie.

sentences.en: And not all ultra-processed foods are hyperpalatable.
sentences.zh: 你在80年代和90年代看到的是，越来越多的超加工食品也变得高度可口。

sentences.en: These are kind of like two different terms, but they overlap a lot.

sentences.en: And what you see in the 1980s and 1990s is that more and more of these ultra-processed foods were also hyperpalatable.

sentences.en: And that seemed to be driven by the tobacco companies.

sentences.en: They were maybe a little bit ahead of the other companies in cracking that hyperpalatability code.

sentences.en: But by the 2010s, basically, all of the food companies kind of get on board and bring their products up to speed.

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: So, it's become a huge problem.

sentences.en: And we see the same thing happening in countries all around the world, although we may be a leader in this regard.

sentences.en: And so, this is where we turn from a story about the business of food to a story about health and science because scientists are alarmed.
sentences.zh: 是因为我们没有进行足够的锻炼，还是因为我们的营养问题？

sentences.en: They're scrambling to figure out why people around the world are gaining weight.

sentences.zh: 在他的国家，他注意到人们摄入的传统食物（如米饭和豆类）减少了，而更多地摄入方便面和香肠等食物。

sentences.en: But there's this one scientist in Brazil named Carlos Montero who starts to look at this question a little bit differently.
sentences.zh: 因此，在2009年，他创造了“超加工食品”这个术语，并建立了一个系统，将食物从“未加工”分类到“超加工”。

sentences.en: In his country, he notices that people are consuming less traditional foods like rice and beans and more foods like instant noodles and sausages.
sentences.zh: 因此，在创建这个定义时，

sentences.en: And so, in 2009, he is the one who actually coins this term, ultra-processed food, and he creates a system to sort foods from unprocessed to ultra-processed.
sentences.zh: 卡洛斯·蒙泰罗和他的同事们现在能够量化食品系统中来自这些食物的比例，以及它随时间发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: And so, in creating this definition,
sentences.zh: 这使他们能够研究它是否与肥胖有关。

sentences.en: Carlos Montero and his colleagues are now able to quantify how much of the food system is coming from these foods and how has it changed over time.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢你，爱丽丝。

sentences.en: And that allows them to study whether or not it's linked to obesity.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: And they find, indeed, in Brazil, as ultra-processed food consumption goes up, so does obesity.
sentences.zh: 他们确实发现，在巴西，随着超加工食品消费量的增加，肥胖率也随之上升。

sentences.en: Other scientists around the world are like, oh, wow, this is an interesting way of looking at diet and health.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的其他科学家也纷纷表示，哇，这是一种观察饮食与健康之间关系的新颖视角。

sentences.en: And they start to see the same link between ultra-processed foods and obesity, as well as other chronic conditions like type 2 diabetes and cardiovascular disease,
sentences.zh: 他们开始发现超加工食品与肥胖之间存在同样的关联，以及与其他慢性疾病（如2型糖尿病和心血管疾病）之间的联系，

sentences.en: some types of cancer.
sentences.zh: 还有某些类型的癌症。

sentences.en: And so, this appears to be kind of a major breakthrough in our understanding of diet and health.
sentences.zh: 因此，这似乎是我们理解饮食与健康关系方面的一个重大突破。

sentences.en: But proving that ultra-processed food is causing those health conditions turns out to be a lot trickier than you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 但要证明超加工食品确实导致了这些健康问题，结果比你想象的要棘手得多。

sentences.en: Alice, I bit into my ring ding.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝，我咬了一口我的Ring Ding蛋糕。

sentences.en: How is it?
sentences.zh: 味道怎么样？

sentences.en: It's really good.
sentences.zh: 非常好吃。

sentences.en: It is hyper-palatable, like uber-hyper.
sentences.zh: 它口感极佳，简直是超级无敌美味。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我负责编写《纽约时报》游戏中的“Connections”谜题，我非常喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像刚才你们听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com/games 即可开始游玩。

sentences.en: So, Alice, what do you mean when you said it was harder than you'd think to prove that ultra-processed foods cause obesity and other health problems?
sentences.zh: 那么，爱丽丝，你刚才说证明超加工食品导致肥胖和其他健康问题比想象中更难，这是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, this is like the eternal challenge of studying nutrition and health, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就像是研究营养与健康时永恒的挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: You can observe a large number of people.
sentences.zh: 你可以观察大量人群。

sentences.en: You can look at how they eat, and you can look at what health conditions they develop or whether, you know, they develop obesity.
sentences.zh: 你可以观察他们的饮食方式，也可以观察他们患上了什么健康疾病，或者说，你知道，他们是否出现了肥胖。

sentences.en: But proving that it's the food that causes those conditions is really challenging.
sentences.zh: 但要证明是食物导致了这些疾病，确实非常具有挑战性。

sentences.en: In other words, just because people are becoming more obese over time and as a result suffering from diseases like type 2 diabetes,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，仅仅因为人们随着时间的推移变得越来越肥胖，并因此患上2型糖尿病等疾病，

sentences.en: that doesn't necessarily mean that it's the ultra-processed foods that's causing that obesity rise.
sentences.zh: 并不一定意味着是超加工食品导致了肥胖率的上升。

sentences.en: And that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 你说得完全正确。

sentences.en: Diet is really complicated, and then food is just like one of the things that can affect our health, right?
sentences.zh: 饮食非常复杂，而且食物只是影响我们健康的因素之一，对吧？

sentences.en: And you can imagine that people who rely more on ultra-processed foods might also be the same people that are getting less sleep and maybe exercising less or they're under more stress or they're experiencing more poverty or discrimination or less access to health care.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，那些更依赖超加工食品的人，可能同时也睡眠不足、运动较少，或者承受着更大的压力，经历着更多的贫困、歧视，或者难以获得医疗服务。

sentences.en: All of these other factors might contribute to someone's health over the long term.
sentences.zh: 所有这些其他因素都可能长期影响一个人的健康。

sentences.en: So, Alice, how do you isolate the driver of worse health then?
sentences.zh: 那么，爱丽丝，你该如何分离出导致健康状况恶化的驱动因素呢？

sentences.en: How do you go about doing that?
sentences.zh: 你打算怎么做？

sentences.en: So, for that, you really need a different kind of study.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了做到这一点，你确实需要一种不同的研究方法。

sentences.en: You need a clinical trial.
sentences.zh: 你需要进行临床试验。

sentences.en: In a perfect world,
sentences.zh: 在理想的情况下，

sentences.en: you can imagine if you took a large group of people and you randomly divided them into two groups and had one group consuming a diet full of ultra-processed foods.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，如果你找来一大群人，随机将他们分成两组，让其中一组食用充满超加工食品的饮食。

sentences.en: And another group consuming a diet full of ultra-processed foods.
sentences.zh: 而另一组也食用充满超加工食品的饮食。

sentences.en: And you would keep them all living in the same conditions and track them for years and see, you know, who develops obesity, who develops type 2 diabetes.
sentences.zh: 你会让他们在相同的条件下生活，并跟踪他们多年，看看谁出现了肥胖，谁患上了2型糖尿病。

sentences.en: That kind of study is obviously really hard to do over the sort of decades that it takes to develop a chronic health condition.
sentences.zh: 显然，要在发展慢性健康问题所需的几十年时间里进行这种研究是非常困难的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You're not really going to say, hey, 10,000 people, come live in my lab for 10 years and I'm going to control everything and you're going to eat exactly the same thing as that guy.
sentences.zh: 你不可能真的说，嘿，一万人，来我的实验室住上10年，我要控制一切，你们每个人吃的都要和那个人完全一样。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: What you can do, though, is a trial kind of like that, but for a much shorter amount of time.
sentences.zh: 不过，你可以做一种类似的试验，但时间要短得多。

sentences.en: And so there was this small study conducted by a researcher named Kevin Hall.
sentences.zh: 有一项由研究员凯文·霍尔进行的小型研究。

sentences.en: And what he did was recruit 20 adults to come and live at the National Institutes of Health for a month.
sentences.zh: 他招募了20名成年人，让他们在国立卫生研究院（NIH）住了一个月。

sentences.en: And each of those study subjects during their month-long stay at the NIH spent two weeks consuming a diet that was made up of unprocessed foods and two weeks consuming a diet made up of ultra-processed foods.
sentences.zh: 在NIH为期一个月的住宿期间，这些研究对象每人有两周时间食用由未加工食品组成的饮食，另外两周食用由超加工食品组成的饮食。

sentences.en: These diets, they were actually very carefully designed by research dietitians so that they were matched in the number of calories on the plate, the amount of carbohydrates,
sentences.zh: 这些饮食实际上是由研究营养师精心设计的，确保盘子里的卡路里数量、碳水化合物含量、

sentences.en: the amount of fat, the amount of sugar, the amount of sodium.
sentences.zh: 脂肪含量、糖分含量和钠含量都是匹配的。

sentences.en: So they really wanted to try to isolate this ultra-processed factor from the actual nutrition provided in these meals.
sentences.zh: 所以他们确实想尝试将超加工因素与这些餐食提供的实际营养分离开来。

sentences.en: And they told the study participants that they could consume as much or as little as they wanted of these foods that were placed in front of them.
sentences.zh: 他们告诉研究参与者，摆在他们面前的这些食物，他们想吃多少就吃多少。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么结果如何呢？

sentences.en: What did the study end up finding?
sentences.zh: 这项研究最终发现了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think I should say first, too,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我首先应该说，

sentences.en: that Kevin Hall went into this study thinking that they would find no difference in how much people consumed or whether or not they gained weight during their time at the NIH.
sentences.zh: 凯文·霍尔在进行这项研究时，认为他们不会发现人们在NIH期间的食物摄入量或体重增加方面有任何差异。

sentences.en: Because the diets were so carefully matched for nutrition,
sentences.zh: 因为这些饮食在营养方面匹配得非常仔细，

sentences.en: he thought that was the thing that really mattered and there wasn't really anything to this ultra-processed concept affecting people's food consumption or health.
sentences.zh: 他认为这才是真正重要的，而超加工概念对人们的食物消费或健康并没有什么影响。

sentences.en: But what he found shocked him and shocked, I think, a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 但他发现的结果让他感到震惊，我想也让很多人感到震惊。

sentences.en: He found that while people were on the ultra-processed diet, they gained two pounds in two weeks.
sentences.zh: 他发现，当人们食用超加工饮食时，两周内体重增加了两磅。

sentences.en: And they ate 500 more calories per day than they did when they were on the unprocessed diet without even realizing it.
sentences.zh: 而且他们每天比食用未加工饮食时多摄入了500卡路里的热量，甚至自己都没有意识到。

sentences.en: Like, they had no idea that they had consumed more food.
sentences.zh: 就像，他们根本不知道自己多吃了食物。

sentences.en: So it's a short-term study.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项短期研究。

sentences.en: You don't know if that amount of sort of overconsumption of calories and weight gain might continue if the study went longer than that.
sentences.zh: 你不知道如果研究时间延长，这种热量摄入过量和体重增加的情况是否会持续下去。

sentences.en: But in that short amount of time, you see this really striking difference in how people responded to these very different types of meals.
sentences.zh: 但在那段短时间内，你可以看到人们对这些截然不同的餐食的反应有着非常显著的差异。

sentences.en: It was very clear that people ate more calories than they needed when they were served these ultra-processed meals.
sentences.zh: 很明显，当人们食用这些超加工餐食时，摄入的热量超过了他们的需求。

sentences.en: Okay, so in a controlled environment, in the perfect scenario, which Kevin Hall created,
sentences.zh: 好的，那么在受控的环境中，在凯文·霍尔创造的完美场景下，

sentences.en: it is true that people do eat more calories and do gain weight from these ultra-processed foods.
sentences.zh: 人们确实会摄入更多热量，并且确实会因为这些超加工食品而体重增加，这是事实。

sentences.en: But do we know exactly why they do, Alice?
sentences.zh: 但我们确切知道原因吗，爱丽丝？

sentences.en: We don't.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道。

sentences.en: Kevin Hall is currently conducting a sunken trial to try to tease that out.
sentences.zh: 凯文·霍尔目前正在进行一项后续试验，试图找出原因。

sentences.en: And he's testing a few different ideas.
sentences.zh: 他正在测试几个不同的想法。

sentences.en: One goes back to that hyper-palatability concept.
sentences.zh: 其中一个回到了“口感极佳”的概念上。

sentences.en: So maybe it's the fact that these foods are more likely to have these pairs of nutrients that light up our brains in rewarding ways and want us to come back and consume more.
sentences.zh: 所以也许是因为这些食物更有可能含有某些营养成分组合，能以奖励的方式激活我们的大脑，让我们想要回来继续食用。

sentences.en: Another is that ultra-processed foods tend to sort of like pack more calories in per bite.
sentences.zh: 另一个原因是超加工食品往往每口包含更多的热量。

sentences.en: And so you might just subconsciously consume more of them because they kind of take up less space in your gut than an unprocessed food.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会在潜意识里摄入更多，因为它们在肠道中占用的空间比未加工食品要小。

sentences.en: If you can make ultra-processed foods that aren't hyper-palatable and don't pack as many calories in per bite, then people do seem to consume less of them.
sentences.zh: 如果你能制造出口感不那么极佳、且每口热量含量较低的超加工食品，那么人们似乎确实会减少摄入量。

sentences.en: So that's what's giving us some hints as to what is going on.
sentences.zh: 所以这为我们提供了一些关于正在发生什么的线索。

sentences.en: These foods are being designed to make us want to eat them and want to eat more of them.
sentences.zh: 这些食物被设计出来，就是为了让我们想吃它们，并且想吃得更多。

sentences.en: Yeah, that certainly seems to be the case.
sentences.zh: 是的，情况似乎确实如此。

sentences.en: And there's another thing about ultra-processed foods that I think scientists worry about and many of us worry about too is that they contain all of these ingredients that we can't pronounce.
sentences.zh: 关于超加工食品，还有一点我认为科学家们很担心，我们许多人也很担心，那就是它们含有所有这些我们念不出名字的成分。

sentences.en: And, you know, it turns out many of them, we don't have a great grasp on how they affect our bodies.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，事实证明，其中许多成分对我们身体的影响，我们并没有很好的了解。

sentences.en: You know, we have like some small studies that show, for example, that artificial food dyes maybe affect children's behavior.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们有一些小型研究表明，例如，人工食用色素可能会影响儿童的行为。

sentences.en: Artificial sweeteners maybe change our microbiomes.
sentences.zh: 人工甜味剂可能会改变我们的微生物群。

sentences.en: You know, some of these other ingredients maybe increase inflammation levels in our bodies.
sentences.zh: 你知道，其他一些成分可能会增加我们体内的炎症水平。

sentences.en: This is really emerging science, but it kind of adds to the sort of accumulated concerns about these industrially made foods.
sentences.zh: 这确实是新兴的科学，但它增加了人们对这些工业制造食品的累积担忧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You should have told me that before the ring ding.
sentences.zh: 你应该在吃那个Ring Ding之前告诉我的。

sentences.en: Sorry, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: Okay, so we know that ultra-processed foods can cause weight gain, at least according to this small study.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们知道超加工食品会导致体重增加，至少根据这项小型研究是这样。

sentences.en: And we're starting to get more research to understand why that happens.
sentences.zh: 我们开始获得更多的研究来了解为什么会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: But why has it taken so long to get to this point?
sentences.zh: 但为什么走到这一步花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: That's another great question.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个好问题。

sentences.en: I mean, nutrition science has been chronically kind of notoriously underfunded by the government.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，营养科学一直以来在政府资助方面都严重不足。

sentences.en: So a lot of nutrition research actually ends up being sponsored by food companies and industry groups themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以很多营养研究最终都是由食品公司和行业团体自己赞助的。

sentences.en: You can imagine that this has not been top of the list for food companies to investigate these effects.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，调查这些影响并不是食品公司的首要任务。

sentences.en: In the United States, about 5% of the National Institutes of Health budget goes towards nutrition research.
sentences.zh: 在美国，国立卫生研究院大约5%的预算用于营养研究。

sentences.en: And I think there's a growing recognition that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们越来越认识到，你知道，

sentences.en: we may need to invest more in understanding this issue if we're going to wrap our heads around what the problem is with these foods and what we could do about it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想弄清楚这些食物的问题所在以及我们能做些什么，我们可能需要投入更多资金来了解这个问题。

sentences.en: What does that growing recognition look like?
sentences.zh: 这种日益增长的认识是什么样的？

sentences.en: What's happening?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think scientists will always say we need more research.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为科学家总是会说我们需要更多的研究。

sentences.en: But we're seeing countries around the world who are saying we know enough to start taking action.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到世界各地的国家都在说，我们知道的已经足够开始采取行动了。

sentences.en: We can't really afford to just let things continue as they are.
sentences.zh: 我们真的负担不起让事情就这样继续下去。

sentences.en: So we're seeing countries, for example, putting prominent warning labels on ultra-processed foods or at least certain ultra-processed foods,
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到各国，例如，在超加工食品或至少某些超加工食品上贴上醒目的警告标签，

sentences.en: like big stop signs that clearly say on the front of the package, this is not a healthy choice.
sentences.zh: 就像包装正面清晰写着的大停车标志一样，这并不是一个健康的选择。

sentences.en: We're seeing countries limit marketing of ultra-processed foods to children.
sentences.zh: 我们看到各国限制向儿童推销超加工食品。

sentences.en: We're seeing them get ultra-processed foods out of school meals.
sentences.zh: 我们看到他们将超加工食品从学校餐食中剔除。

sentences.en: But here in the United States, when I talked to experts about these types of policies a couple years ago,
sentences.zh: 但在美国，几年前我和专家谈论这些类型的政策时，

sentences.en: they said it seems unlikely that a lot of those policies would really take off in the United States because we have a very strong food lobby.
sentences.zh: 他们说这些政策在美国似乎不太可能真正流行起来，因为我们有非常强大的食品游说团体。

sentences.en: But things are really shifting, I think, in this conversation.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这场对话中的情况确实正在发生转变。

sentences.en: We saw it during the presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 我们在总统竞选期间看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Robert F.
sentences.zh: 小罗伯特·F·

sentences.en: Kennedy Jr.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪，

sentences.en: campaigned pretty heavily for himself and then for Trump on this idea of making America healthy again.
sentences.zh: 他大力为自己，后来又为特朗普竞选，主张让美国再次健康起来。

sentences.en: And he talked a lot about ultra-processed foods and the effects that they're having on children's health.
sentences.zh: 他谈了很多关于超加工食品及其对儿童健康的影响。

sentences.en: And I think you saw that resonate with a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 我认为你看到了这引起了许多人的共鸣。

sentences.en: And politicians on both sides of the aisle are taking an interest in this.
sentences.zh: 两党的政客们都对此产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: There was a hearing in the Senate last week where there were no senators who defended big food.
sentences.zh: 上周参议院举行了一场听证会，会上没有参议员为大型食品公司辩护。

sentences.en: It was kind of like, yeah, ultra-processed foods are a problem and we need to change something in this country.
sentences.zh: 情况就像是，是的，超加工食品是个问题，我们需要在这个国家做出改变。

sentences.en: Okay, Alice, here's the part in the podcast where I ask you how you think about these foods because you're the expert.
sentences.zh: 好的，爱丽丝，现在是播客中我问你如何看待这些食物的部分，因为你是专家。

sentences.en: I want to probably try to avoid a lot of these foods and I want to know how you think about doing that given that they're kind of everywhere.
sentences.zh: 我可能想尝试避免食用很多这类食物，我想知道考虑到它们随处可见，你对此有什么看法。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's really tough.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这真的很难。

sentences.en: And we are, again, talking about 70% of the food supply.
sentences.zh: 而且我们再次谈论的是占食品供应70%的比例。

sentences.en: And a lot of these foods I, as a parent, do rely on.
sentences.zh: 作为一名家长，我也确实依赖很多这类食物。

sentences.en: Things like breakfast cereal, honey nut Cheerios my kids eat occasionally.
sentences.zh: 比如早餐麦片，我孩子们偶尔吃的蜂蜜坚果Cheerios。

sentences.en: But here's what I would say.
sentences.zh: 但我会说的是：

sentences.en: We're still learning a lot.
sentences.zh: 我们仍在学习很多东西。

sentences.en: And one of the things we really don't know is whether or not all of these foods in this huge category of ultra-processed foods are bad for us.
sentences.zh: 我们真正不知道的一件事是，在这个巨大的超加工食品类别中，是否所有的食物都对我们有害。

sentences.en: Like just because they're industrially produced, are they unhealthy?
sentences.zh: 就像仅仅因为它们是工业化生产的，它们就不健康吗？

sentences.en: Probably not.
sentences.zh: 可能不是。

sentences.en: And we're talking about a category that includes everything from soda to whole wheat bread.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论的是一个涵盖从苏打水到全麦面包的所有类别的食物。

sentences.en: So the way I think about them is I'm looking at sort of degrees of ultra-processing.
sentences.zh: 所以我看待它们的方式是观察超加工的程度。

sentences.en: Like if it's a whole wheat bread, that the only thing that makes it ultra-processed is the inclusion of like one food additive that I don't recognize.
sentences.zh: 比如如果是全麦面包，它唯一超加工的地方就是添加了一种我不认识的食品添加剂。

sentences.en: I'm less concerned about that.
sentences.zh: 我对此就不那么担心。

sentences.en: I think try to sort out the sort of worst offenders, which are sugary drinks, ultra-processed.
sentences.zh: 我认为要尝试找出最糟糕的违规者，即含糖饮料，它们是超加工的。

sentences.en: To me, it's like hot dogs and chicken nuggets and then foods that obviously don't provide us with very much nutrition and are difficult to stop eating.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，就像热狗和鸡块，以及那些显然不能为我们提供太多营养且让人难以停止食用的食物。

sentences.en: Those are my kind of red flags for the ultra-processed foods I'm going to try to avoid.
sentences.zh: 这些是我要尽量避免的超加工食品的红线。

sentences.en: Thinking about the future of this problem, Alice, I wonder if an analogy is the tobacco companies in the beginning of the conversation and the cigarette industry, right?
sentences.zh: 考虑到这个问题的未来，爱丽丝，我想知道这是否可以类比为对话开始时的烟草公司和香烟行业，对吧？

sentences.en: That back in the beginning, the industry was incredibly well-funded.
sentences.zh: 在最初的时候，这个行业资金极其雄厚。

sentences.en: It was very difficult for scientists to prove that cigarettes were in fact bad for you.
sentences.zh: 科学家很难证明香烟确实对你有害。

sentences.en: But eventually they did, and eventually they were regulated.
sentences.zh: 但最终他们做到了，最终它们受到了监管。

sentences.en: And I wonder in some way if ultra-processed food might also follow that same trajectory, but just kind of be at the beginning of it right now.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，超加工食品是否也会以某种方式遵循同样的轨迹，只是现在还处于起步阶段。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's quite possible.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这很有可能。

sentences.en: I'm seeing more and more addiction scientists who traditionally have studied substances like tobacco and alcohol now turning their attention to foods and trying to really understand the potentially addictive nature of foods.
sentences.zh: 我看到越来越多的成瘾科学家，他们传统上研究烟草和酒精等物质，现在开始关注食物，并试图真正了解食物潜在的成瘾性。

sentences.en: But it's a bit harder with food, right?
sentences.zh: 但食物的情况有点复杂，对吧？

sentences.en: Because we don't need cigarettes and we can isolate from cigarettes the addictive substance, which is nicotine.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不需要香烟，而且我们可以从香烟中分离出成瘾物质，即尼古丁。

sentences.en: Food is different, right?
sentences.zh: 食物则不同，对吧？

sentences.en: Like we all need to eat and ultra-processed foods are convenient and feed many of us with like the calories that we need every day.
sentences.zh: 我们都需要吃饭，而超加工食品很方便，为我们许多人提供了每天所需的热量。

sentences.en: So proving that there's an addictive nature to some foods is a bit more challenging, but there are a lot of scientists now who have taken an interest in that and are working on it.
sentences.zh: 所以证明某些食物具有成瘾性更具挑战性，但现在有很多科学家对此产生了兴趣，并正在研究它。

sentences.en: So I think we may be moving in that direction.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们可能正在朝着那个方向发展。

sentences.en: And there is a growing sense that, you know, this helps us make sense of the problem that we're facing, this rise in obesity.
sentences.zh: 而且人们越来越意识到，你知道，这有助于我们理解我们正面临的问题，即肥胖率的上升。

sentences.en: For a long time, it's been talked about as a personal failing, like people are not exercising enough and they're eating too much.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，这都被视为一种个人缺陷，仿佛是人们锻炼得不够，吃得太多。

sentences.en: And, you know, if we're talking about living in an environment where we're surrounded by foods that are difficult to stop eating because they've been engineered that way,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果我们谈论的是生活在一个被各种让人欲罢不能的食物所包围的环境中，因为它们就是被这样设计出来的，

sentences.en: it sort of changes the way you think about the problem and opens the door, I think, for more solutions.
sentences.zh: 这在某种程度上改变了你对这个问题的看法，我认为，这也为更多的解决方案打开了大门。

sentences.en: Like if we could change the environment so that it's not so saturated with foods that are hard to stop eating, then we may have a chance of turning the tide on obesity.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果我们能改变这种环境，让它不再充斥着那些让人难以停口的食物，那么我们或许就有机会扭转肥胖症的趋势。

sentences.en: Alice, thank you.
sentences.zh: 爱丽丝，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Thursday, President Biden said that he was commuting the sentences of nearly 1,500 people and pardoning 39 people in a sweeping act of clemency during his final weeks in office.
sentences.zh: 周四，拜登总统表示，在他任期的最后几周里，他将采取大规模的宽大处理行动，为近1500人减刑，并赦免39人。

sentences.en: The White House said that it was the largest number of commutations by an American president in a single day.
sentences.zh: 白宫表示，这是美国总统在单日内减刑人数最多的一次。

sentences.en: The commutations affect those who have been released from prison and placed in home confinement during the coronavirus pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这些减刑措施针对的是那些在新冠疫情期间从监狱获释并被安置在居家监禁中的人。

sentences.en: The pardons are for people who were convicted of nonviolent crimes, including drug offenses.
sentences.zh: 赦免的对象是那些被判犯有非暴力罪行的人，包括毒品犯罪。

sentences.en: As a senator, Biden had championed a 1994 crime bill that many experts say fueled mass incarceration.
sentences.zh: 作为参议员，拜登曾力推1994年的犯罪法案，许多专家认为该法案助长了大规模监禁。

sentences.en: He has since expressed regret for supporting that legislation.
sentences.zh: 此后，他已对支持该立法表示遗憾。

sentences.en: And he committed during the 2020 campaign to addressing the long drug sentences that resulted.
sentences.zh: 并且他在2020年竞选期间承诺要解决由此导致的长期毒品刑罚问题。

sentences.en: The announcement came two weeks after Biden issued a pardon for his son, Hunter, a decision that was harshly criticized by both Republicans and Democrats.
sentences.zh: 这一宣布是在拜登赦免其子亨特两周后发布的，该决定遭到了共和党和民主党双方的严厉批评。

sentences.en: A quick reminder to catch a new episode of The Interview right here tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 温馨提醒，明天请继续锁定这里收看新一期的《访谈》。

sentences.en: This week, Lulu Garcia Navarro talks with travel guru Rick Steves about why he spent his life encouraging Americans to get outside their comfort zones.
sentences.zh: 本周，露露·加西亚·纳瓦罗与旅游达人瑞克·史蒂夫斯探讨了他为何毕生致力于鼓励美国人走出舒适区。

sentences.en: You just feel so good, and you just feel like this world is such a beautiful place, and it's filled with beautiful people, and nature is so fragile,
sentences.zh: 你会感觉非常好，你会觉得这个世界是如此美丽，充满了美好的人们，而大自然又是如此脆弱，

sentences.en: and it's just such a delight and a blessing.
sentences.zh: 这真是一种愉悦和福分。

sentences.en: It changes you.
sentences.zh: 它会改变你。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Alex Stern, Sidney Harper, and Ricky Nevetsky, with help from Olivia Nat and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由亚历克斯·斯特恩、西德尼·哈珀和瑞奇·内维茨基制作，奥利维亚·纳特和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊提供了协助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow and Chris Haxel, contains original music by Dan Powell and Marion Lozano, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 节目由丽莎·周和克里斯·哈克塞尔编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和马里昂·洛萨诺的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Landsberg of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Taverdisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗迪西。

sentences.en: See you on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称为改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何平台收听。
